summary: The SpatioTemporal Asset Catalog is a community specification for describing and searching files that represent the Earth at a place and time, such as satellite and drone imagery, elevation models and lidar point clouds. It defines small catalogue, collection and item records that point to the files and carry a footprint, a time, a licence and descriptive properties, and it can be extended with named add-ons; a companion web interface specification adds search by place, time and collection. It covers discovery, coverage, licence, versioning and descriptive metadata of geospatial data well. It does not define how any asset is encoded or drawn, and it has nothing on scenes, avatars, identity, networking or sessions, which it leaves to the file formats it points to and to other standards. A standards audience should know that the search interface specification is versioned separately (1.0.0) from the core specification (1.1.0), and that useful fields for point clouds and tiling live in community extensions of varying maturity, with the tiling one still at proposal stage. A catalogue entry tells a client that a point cloud or three-dimensional file exists and where; it does not guarantee that a spatial runtime can load it.

coverage.note: Every Item carries a free-form properties dictionary, the common metadata fields and community extensions with published JSON Schemas give those properties a declared structure, and Collections can summarise them.
